1. Service governance, portfolio and value
Service governance, portfolio, value and performance

NDIA must govern each ICT service through a defined owner, delegated decision rights, service purpose, portfolio roadmap, transition approval, performance measures and benefits evidence that support executive, Board and whole-of-government reporting.

NDIA must have a named owner for every ICT service. The owner must define the service purpose, expected value, performance measures, roadmap and decision points, and must keep evidence that the service is meeting business, participant and government reporting needs.
Service governance requirement
High

2. Risk, assurance and integrity controls
Risk management, assurance, internal control and fraud prevention

ICT service risks, including security, shared, supplier, residual, fraud and corruption risks, must be identified, assessed, assigned, treated, tested, monitored and reported within NDIA risk appetite, with exceptions and control gaps formally accepted and tracked.

NDIA must manage risks for every ICT service. Service owners must identify, assess, treat and report security, supplier, fraud, control and residual risks, and must record who accepts any risk that remains.
Risk and assurance requirement

ICT services must be designed, delivered and improved around participant and user needs, accessibility, inclusion, safe digital experience, reliable support channels and reasonable alternatives where digital access is unsuitable.

4. Information protection, privacy and lawful handling
Protected information, personal information, privacy and lawful disclosure

ICT services must protect classified, caveated, protected, personal and critical infrastructure information by applying lawful collection, access, use, disclosure, sharing, privacy governance, PIA, metadata, consent, security and disposal controls.

NDIA must protect personal, protected, classified and critical information handled by ICT services. Information must only be collected, accessed, used, shared, retained and disposed of where it is lawful, authorised, secure and auditable.
Information protection and privacy requirement

6. Supplier, procurement and contract management
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party assurance

ICT procurement and supplier arrangements must define and monitor value-for-money, security, privacy, accessibility, fraud, continuity, incident reporting, assurance, subcontractor, exit, performance and service-level obligations throughout the supplier lifecycle.

NDIA must manage ICT suppliers from planning to exit. Contracts and service arrangements must clearly state security, privacy, accessibility, continuity, performance, reporting and assurance obligations, and NDIA must monitor whether suppliers meet them.
